A large service often relies on dense, tightly coupled internal meshes for redundancy, which allows a localized fault to cascade globally. A decentralized network can be explicitly architected with high clustering and weak ties between clusters. This creates a 'small-world' modular topology where local failures remain isolated because the weak ties do not transmit the high-bandwidth failure signal.
